title: Dabur's September-quarter profit rises 11.7% to Rs 505 crore as volumes grow 5.5%
dek: Revenue rose 11.6% to Rs 3,563 crore and the international business grew 20%, but operating margins narrowed as input costs rose. The board declared an interim dividend of Rs 3.50 a share.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Dabur India, the maker of Dabur Chyawanprash, Real juices and Vatika hair oil, said on Wednesday that its net profit for July-September rose 11.7% from a year earlier to Rs 505.5 crore. Revenue rose 11.6%.

The company reported the results after the market closed. Consolidated revenue from operations was Rs 3,563.07 crore, up from Rs 3,191.32 crore a year earlier, according to the figures reported by Business Today. Profit attributable to shareholders a year earlier was Rs 452.55 crore. This is the second quarter in a row of double-digit revenue growth, and the fourth in a row of double-digit profit growth.

## Where the growth came from

In India, Dabur's fast-moving consumer goods business grew 10.7%. Underlying volume growth was 5.5%. Volume growth strips out price increases, so it shows how many more units the company sold.

By category:

- home and personal care grew 10.9%, led by hair oils and shampoos and double-digit growth in home care
- food and beverages grew 17.4%
- healthcare grew 6.9%, with digestives and over-the-counter medicines growing in double digits

The company said its premium brands grew four times as fast as its regular ones and now make up 20% of the domestic business. The international business grew 20% in rupee terms.

## Margins under pressure

Operating profit (EBITDA) rose 7.5% to Rs 633 crore, slower than revenue, and the operating margin narrowed by 60 basis points (0.6 percentage points). Chief executive Herjit S. Bhalla said the company had delivered "profitable growth" in a difficult environment. He pointed to geopolitical uncertainty and higher input costs, and said growth was broad-based and backed by healthy volumes.

The board declared an interim dividend of Rs 3.50 a share for the year. The record date is 10 November, and payments begin on 25 November.

## How it compares

This quarter's growth is a clear step up from a year ago. In July-September 2025, Dabur's net profit rose 6.5% to Rs 453 crore and revenue grew 5.4%, Upstox reported at the time. EBITDA that quarter was Rs 588 crore, a margin of 18.43%.

The first quarter of this financial year, April-June, was also strong. Net profit rose 15% to Rs 591 crore and revenue rose 10.5% to Rs 3,764 crore, Kotak Neo reported when those results came out in July. Both profit and revenue in the latest quarter were lower than in April-June. Last year followed the same pattern: profit of Rs 514 crore in the June quarter was followed by Rs 453 crore in July-September.

## Shares

Dabur's shares closed 3.45% higher at Rs 394.10 on the BSE on Wednesday, before the results were announced, according to Business Today. Thursday's trading will be the first chance for investors to react to the numbers.

The figures here are as reported by Business Today. The Declaration has not yet seen the company's stock-exchange filing.
